_defect: A workflow `run:` block that READS a PowerShell variable it never ASSIGNS. Every GitHub Actions `run:` block is a separate shell process, so a variable assigned in an earlier step is $null here. windows-validation.yml's param-id reconciliation step read $outDir and $testExe that way; `Join-Path $null` threw a mandatory-parameter binding error, so the step died on its first line on every run it ever made, and its two reconciliation layers -- built to catch PDF-79's seventeen phantom parameterised cases -- had never once executed.
_ratchet: TWO-WAY. An unadjudicated new finding FAILS, and an adjudicated entry that has stopped being a finding also FAILS, so this file cannot quietly drift out of step with the tree.
_empty_on_purpose: There are currently ZERO findings, and that is a measured result rather than an unused file. The guard's first real-mode run found four: the one true positive in windows-validation.yml (fixed in the same commit, mutation-verified -- removing the three derivation lines makes the guard flag $outDir and $testExe again) and three FALSE positives in windows-fuzz.yml. The false positives were FIXED IN THE DETECTOR, not adjudicated here: `function Get-ArtifactVerdict([string]$binPath, [string]$artifactPath)` is an inline function parameter list rather than `param(...)`, and `Tee-Object -Variable campaignOut` binds a name under the bare `-Variable` spelling. Both forms are now recognised and both are pinned in --self-test. Adjudicating a false positive as debt would have hidden the real class behind a file that looked like progress.
_how_to_adjudicate: Add "<file>|<job>|<step name>|<variable>": "<reason>". A reason is mandatory and should say why the read is correct despite not being assigned in the block -- for example a variable bound through indirection (Set-Variable -Name (...), New-Variable), which this lexical analysis cannot see. Prefer fixing the detector when the finding is wrong, and prefer deriving the variable in the block when the finding is right.
_scope_limits: pwsh/powershell steps only (this is a PowerShell scoping rule). Lexical, not a PowerShell parser. Single-quoted strings and single-quoted here-strings are stripped because PowerShell does not interpolate them; double-quoted forms are scanned. ${{ }} is stripped as a GitHub expression. Function parameters are treated as assigned for the whole block, so a read of one OUTSIDE its function is deliberately not reported -- over-reporting correct code is what gets a guard switched off.
